title: Macie, Config & Compliance Evidence
summary: Find sensitive data, track configuration compliance and collect audit evidence.
tldr: **Macie** finds PII and other sensitive data **in S3 objects**. Turn on automated sensitive data discovery from a delegated administrator to cover a whole organization.
**AWS Config** records resource configuration over time and evaluates it against rules. A **conformance pack** bundles rules and remediations and can be deployed organization-wide.
**Audit Manager** collects evidence about *your* resources and maps it to frameworks such as PCI DSS. **AWS Artifact** hands you *AWS's own* reports and agreements (SOC, PCI AoC, BAA).

keyFacts.text: A Macie **custom data identifier** combines a regular expression with optional keywords that must appear near the match, for formats Macie doesn't know.
Macie, Config conformance packs and Audit Manager all support a **delegated administrator** account so one team can manage every account in AWS Organizations.
Config rules can trigger **Systems Manager Automation** documents to fix noncompliant resources automatically, such as turning on S3 versioning.
Accepting the **AWS Organizations BAA** in Artifact Agreements from the management account covers all member accounts at once.
A **CloudWatch Logs data protection policy** masks sensitive values in log events. Only principals with `logs:Unmask` can see the original values.

keywords.answer: Macie automated sensitive data discovery with a delegated administrator

keywords.cue: company-specific ID pattern Macie doesn't detect
keywords.answer: Macie custom data identifier (regex plus keywords)

keywords.cue: single deployable package of rules and remediations for all accounts

keywords.answer: Config rule with SSM Automation remediation

give a customer AWS's SOC 2 report
accept a BAA for every account in the organization
keywords.answer: AWS Artifact Agreements from the management account

keywords.cue: mask emails and card numbers in CloudWatch logs

traps: **GuardDuty** detects threats and suspicious activity. It does not classify the data inside S3 objects; that is Macie.
AWS Config evaluates *configuration*, not *content*. A Config rule can't tell you whether a bucket holds PII.
Downloading AWS's compliance report from Artifact proves AWS's side only. Evidence about your own resources comes from Audit Manager.
Security Hub compliance standards report on controls. Enabling one is never a BAA with AWS.
Encrypting a log group with KMS doesn't hide values from people who can read the logs. Use a data protection policy to mask them.
